title: 10 Best Luxury Family Resorts with Exceptional Kids Clubs in Asia
excerpt: Not all kids clubs are created equal. We've evaluated kids' programs across Asia's top luxury resorts — from marine biology labs in the Maldives to Balinese dance classes in Ubud. Here are the 10 that truly delight children while giving parents peace of mind.
author: The Luxury Explorer
content:
The Rise of the Exceptional Kids Club

The days of a simple sandbox and a babysitter are long gone. Asia's best luxury resorts have transformed their kids' clubs into immersive educational experiences that rival the finest schools. From marine biology labs to organic farming programmes, these clubs keep children engaged, inspired, and — most importantly — happy while parents enjoy some well-deserved time together.

1. Soneva Fushi — The Den (Maldives)

Soneva Fushi's kids' club is legendary — and for good reason. Housed in a whimsical structure that looks like a giant bamboo manta ray, The Den offers everything from chocolate-making classes (the famous Chocolate Room is open to kids) to astronomy sessions in the on-site observatory. The ratio of carers to children is exceptional, and the programme is tailored by age group so toddlers and teenagers each have age-appropriate adventures. Best for: Families who want their children to learn while having fun.

2. Four Seasons Sayan — Cultural Immersion (Bali)

The kids' club at Four Seasons Sayan takes full advantage of its Ubud setting. Children learn to make Balinese offerings from palm leaves, participate in rice planting alongside local farmers, and take traditional dance lessons from temple dancers. The club is open from 9am to 9pm, and the staff-to-child ratio never exceeds 1:4. Parents love the WhatsApp updates with photos throughout the day.

3. Amanpuri — The Beach Club (Phuket)

Amanpuri's approach to kids' activities is characteristically understated but remarkably effective. The beach club offers Thai boxing classes for children aged 8+, snorkeling excursions to nearby coral reefs, and Thai cooking classes where kids learn to make pad thai and mango sticky rice. Younger children enjoy sandcastle competitions and treasure hunts on the private beach. Best for: Families who want unstructured luxury with optional activities.

4. Velaa Private Island — Marine Biology Programme (Maldives)

Velaa's kids' club is one of the few in the world with a dedicated marine biology programme. Children aged 6-12 can participate in coral planting, manta ray identification, and guided reef snorkels with the resort's resident marine biologist. The club also offers Maldivian language lessons, coconut husking demonstrations, and evening storytelling sessions. Best for: Budding marine biologists and curious minds.

5. Trisara — The Turtle Club (Phuket)

Trisara's Turtle Club is divided into age-appropriate zones: a dedicated baby room with cribs and soft play for under-3s, an adventure zone for 4-8 year olds with art and cooking, and a teen hangout with gaming consoles and table tennis. The outdoor area features a splash pool, slide, and jungle playhouse. Evening babysitting is included for guests in pool villas.

6. The Datai Langkawi — Nature Discovery (Malaysia)

Set within 10 million year-old rainforest, The Datai's kids' club focuses on nature discovery. Children join resident naturalists on jungle walks, learn about the endangered flying lemur, plant mangrove seedlings, and search for orchid species. The club also offers batik painting, traditional kite-making, and Malay language lessons. Best for: Nature-loving families.

7. Capella Singapore — The Explorers Club (Singapore)

Capella Singapore's Explorers Club offers a cosmopolitan programme that reflects its location. Children can take part in bird-watching walks through the resort's 30-acre grounds, Peranakan cooking classes, and heritage tours of the colonial buildings. The club also offers evening movie nights under the stars and a dedicated teen programme with e-sports.

8. Cheval Blanc Randheli — Le Carrousel (Maldives)

True to its LVMH heritage, Cheval Blanc's kids' club is exceptionally stylish — but more importantly, it's exceptionally well-run. Children receive a welcome gift of their own pareo and hat, then choose from activities including coconut painting, Maldivian dancing, and guided snorkeling. The club is open until 10pm, and in-room babysitting is available at no extra charge for villa guests.

9. Four Seasons Hong Kong — Urban Explorers

As an urban property, Four Seasons Hong Kong offers a different kind of kids' club experience: curated city adventures. Children can visit Hong Kong's best family attractions with a dedicated nanny, participate in dim sum-making classes with the pastry chef, or enjoy in-room movie nights with custom menus. The club itself features a play area with Hong Kong-themed toys and books.

10. Ayana Estate — Seven Pools Adventure (Bali)

Ayana Estate's kids' club is one of the most comprehensive in Bali, spread across the resort's 90-hectare property. Children aged 4-12 can enjoy the seven-pool complex (including a dedicated kids' pool with waterslides), participate in Balinese cooking classes, make traditional offerings, and join guided beach walks to discover marine life. Teenagers have their own programme including e-sports and photography workshops.

What to Look For in a Kids Club

When evaluating kids' clubs, consider these five factors: staff-to-child ratio (1:4 or better is ideal), hours of operation (9am-9pm is standard for top properties), age-appropriate programming (toddlers and teenagers need different activities), safety protocols (all staff should be first-aid trained), and flexibility (the best clubs allow drop-in participation without advance booking). Our top recommendation: Soneva Fushi's The Den is the gold standard, but Four Seasons Sayan offers the most culturally immersive experience.
